passage: For the past two weeks, building work on a site near your home has been continuing late into the night.
question:
Write a letter to your local council.

In your letter
• describe the building work and when it takes place
• explain how it is affecting you and your family
• say what you would like the council to do

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the construction work taking place on the former car park on Linden Road, directly opposite my house.

For the past two weeks, workers have been operating heavy machinery, including a concrete mixer and a drill, until around midnight on weekdays. On several occasions, lorries have also arrived to unload materials as late as 11.30 pm, with their engines running and reverse alarms sounding.

This noise is having a serious effect on my family. My two young children are being woken up repeatedly, and they are tired and irritable at school the next day. My husband, who starts work at 6 am, is getting very little sleep, and I am finding it hard to concentrate when I work from home.

I would therefore be grateful if the council could check whether the company has permission to work at night. If it does not, I would ask you to make sure that work stops by 7 pm, as I understand is normal for residential areas.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Amira Haddad
explanation: 3 つの 指示（工事の 内容と 時間・家族への 影響・市への 要望）を 1 段落ずつ 具体的に 書いており Task Achievement が 満たされている。Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully の 正しい 組み合わせと、I would be grateful if… など 丁寧な フォーマル表現が 評価される。

passage: Your sister is graduating from university in another country, and you would like to attend the ceremony.
question:
Write a letter to your manager.

In your letter
• explain why you need time off
• say how your work will be covered while you are away
• suggest the dates you would like to take off

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Ms Lindqvist,
answer:
Dear Ms Lindqvist,

I am writing to ask whether I could take two days of annual leave next month.

My younger sister, Mei, is graduating from her university in Melbourne on Friday 14 March. She is the first person in our family to complete a degree, so the ceremony means a great deal to all of us, and my parents are hoping that the whole family can be there.

I have already spoken to Daniel in our team, and he has kindly agreed to deal with any urgent customer enquiries while I am away. Before I leave, I will also finish the monthly sales report, which is normally due that week, and I will leave clear notes on my other ongoing tasks. In addition, I will check my emails once a day in case anything important comes up.

Ideally, I would like to take Thursday 13 and Friday 14 March off, returning to work on Monday 17 March. If those dates are inconvenient, I would be happy to discuss alternatives.

Thank you for considering my request.

Kind regards,
Lin Zhao
explanation: 上司宛ての セミフォーマルな 手紙として、理由・代わりの 体制・希望日を 具体的な 日付と 名前で 示している。If those dates are inconvenient… と 代案に 触れる 配慮が 語調（tone）の 適切さとして 評価される。

passage: Last month you stayed with a host family while you were studying English abroad.
question:
Write a letter to the family.

In your letter
• thank them for having you
• describe what you enjoyed most during your stay
• invite them to visit you in your country

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mr and Mrs Okafor,
answer:
Dear Mr and Mrs Okafor,

I hope you are both well. I arrived home safely last week, and I wanted to write to say a big thank you for looking after me so well during my month in Brighton.

You made me feel like part of the family from the first day. I know it is not easy to have a stranger living in your home, but you were always patient with my English and you helped me a lot with my homework.

The thing I enjoyed most was our Sunday dinners. I loved trying your traditional dishes, and I really liked the evenings when we played board games together afterwards. I also enjoyed our trip to the countryside, especially the walk along the cliffs. It was the most beautiful place I visited during my stay.

I would be very happy if you could come and visit me in Japan one day. My family would love to meet you, and I could show you around Kyoto. Spring is a good time to come because of the cherry blossoms.

Thank you again for everything.

Best wishes,
Haruto

passage: A local museum is looking for volunteers to help at its weekend family events.
question:
Write a letter to the museum.

In your letter
• introduce yourself
• explain why you are interested in volunteering
• describe the skills you have and when you are available

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing in response to your advertisement for volunteers to help at the museum's weekend family events. I am a 24-year-old graduate in history, and I currently work part-time as a tour guide in the old town.

I have been a regular visitor to the museum since I was a child, and I believe it plays an important role in helping young people develop an interest in the past. Volunteering would be an excellent opportunity for me to give something back to the community while also gaining experience, as I hope to work in museum education in the future.

I think I have several skills that would be useful. Through my work as a guide, I have become confident speaking to groups of all ages, and I am used to explaining historical events in a simple and lively way. I also speak French and Arabic, which could be helpful for visiting families.

I am available every Saturday and on two Sundays a month, and I could also help during the school holidays.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Samir Benali

passage: You are going to move to a new city because of a change in your job.
question:
Write a letter to a friend.

In your letter
• explain why you are moving
• describe your new home
• suggest when your friend could come and visit you

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Tomás,
answer:
Dear Tomás,

I hope everything is going well with you and that you're enjoying your new running club. I've got some big news: I'm moving to Rotterdam at the end of next month!

As you know, I've been working for the same engineering company for five years. A few weeks ago, my boss offered me a position as a project manager in our office there. It's a real step up in my career, and the salary is much better, so I couldn't say no, even though I'll miss everyone here.

I've already found a flat to rent. It's on the third floor of an old brick building right next to a canal, and it has a small balcony where I can sit in the evenings. It's not huge – just one bedroom and an open-plan kitchen and living room – but it's bright and only a ten-minute bike ride from the office.

Once I've settled in, you must come and stay. How about the second weekend of June? The weather should be nice by then, and there's a music festival in the city that I think you'd love. You can sleep on the sofa bed!

Write back soon.

Love,
Ingrid

passage: The heating in the flat you rent has stopped working.
question:
Write a letter to your landlord.

In your letter
• describe the problem
• explain what you have already done about it
• say what you would like the landlord to do and when

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mr Petrov,
answer:
Dear Mr Petrov,

I am writing to let you know about a problem with the heating in my flat at 12B Elm Court.

Since last Thursday, the radiators in all the rooms have been completely cold, and the boiler keeps displaying a red warning light. There is still hot water in the taps, but without heating, the temperature inside the flat has dropped to around 13 degrees at night, which is very uncomfortable now that winter has started.

I have tried to solve the problem myself by following the instructions in the boiler manual. I restarted the boiler twice and checked the pressure, which seemed to be lower than it should be. I also tried to contact you by phone on Friday and Monday, but I was unable to reach you, so I left two voicemail messages.

I would be grateful if you could arrange for a qualified engineer to inspect and repair the boiler as soon as possible, ideally by the end of this week. I am at home every morning before 10 am, so the engineer could visit then.

Thank you in advance for your help.

Yours sincerely,
Grace Mensah
explanation: 問題の 症状・自分で 試した こと・期限つきの 依頼 を それぞれ 具体的に 書いており、3 つの 指示を 完全に カバーしている。Dear Mr Petrov → Yours sincerely の 正しい 結び と、過去形・現在完了の 使い分けの 正確さが 文法点を 上げる。

passage: A friend is planning to visit your city with his parents and has asked you to recommend a restaurant.
question:
Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter
• describe the restaurant you recommend
• explain why it would suit your friend and his parents
• give some advice about booking and getting there

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Kofi,
answer:
Dear Kofi,

It was great to hear that you're coming to visit with your parents next month! You asked me to recommend somewhere to eat, and I know exactly the place.

It's a family-run restaurant called Casa Lume, in the old harbour area. It specialises in seafood and traditional local dishes, and everything is made with fresh ingredients from the market that morning. The dining room is in an old stone warehouse, with big windows looking out over the fishing boats, so the atmosphere is lovely, especially at sunset.

I think it would suit your parents perfectly. It's quiet enough to have a proper conversation, unlike a lot of the trendy places in the centre, and the staff are very friendly and patient. There are also plenty of vegetarian options, which is good because I remember your mum doesn't eat meat. Prices are reasonable, too.

It's very popular, so I'd book a table at least a week in advance – you can do it online. As for getting there, take the number 4 tram to Harbour Square; it's only a two-minute walk from the stop.

Enjoy your trip!

All the best,
Lucía
explanation: 推薦の 手紙として 店の 描写 → 両親に 合う 理由 → 予約と 行き方 と 指示の 順に 書かれている。相手の 母親が ベジタリアン という 個人的な 情報を 入れる など、読み手を 意識した 内容が Task Achievement と 語調の 適切さに つながる。

passage: Yesterday you visited a public library and left a bag behind in the reading room.
question:
Write a letter to the library manager.

In your letter
• describe the bag and what was inside it
• explain when and where you think you left it
• say how the library can contact you

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing because I left my bag in your library yesterday, and I would be very grateful for your help in finding it.

The bag is a small dark green backpack with a brown leather strap and a badge of a mountain on the front pocket. Inside it there is a blue notebook with my university notes, a pencil case, a black umbrella and a water bottle. The notebook is very important to me because it contains all my handwritten notes for my exams next month.

I visited the library on Tuesday afternoon, between about 2 pm and 5 pm. I was sitting at one of the long tables in the reading room on the first floor, near the windows. I think I put the bag under my chair and then forgot to take it when I left in a hurry to catch my bus.

If anyone finds the bag, please contact me by phone on 07700 900184 or by email at r.costa@example.com. I can come to collect it at any time.

Thank you very much for your help.

Yours faithfully,
Rafael Costa
explanation: Band 5.5〜6 の 目安：特徴（色・バッジ・中身）と 場所・時間が 具体的で、指示は すべて 満たしている。文は シンプルだが 誤りが 少なく、フォーマルな 書き出しと 結びも 正しく 使えている。

passage: You recently paid for an online course, but it was very different from the description on the website.
question:
Write a letter to the company that runs the course.

In your letter
• give details of the course you paid for
• explain how the course was different from the description
• say what you would like the company to do

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to request a refund for the online course "Practical Spanish for Business", which I purchased from your website on 2 September for €180.

According to the course description, the programme consisted of twelve live video lessons with a qualified teacher, weekly speaking practice in small groups and personalised feedback on written assignments. These features were the main reason I chose your course over cheaper alternatives.

Unfortunately, the course I received bore little resemblance to this description. Instead of live lessons, there were pre-recorded videos, several of which had poor sound quality. The group speaking sessions were cancelled twice without notice, and on the one occasion they took place, there were over thirty participants, which made meaningful practice impossible. Furthermore, I have submitted three written assignments, yet I have not received any feedback whatsoever.

Given that the course clearly failed to deliver what was advertised, I would ask you to refund the full amount within fourteen days. I would also appreciate a written explanation of why the course content was changed.

I look forward to your prompt reply.

Yours faithfully,
Nadia Rahimi
explanation: 広告内容と 実際の ちがいを 3 点 対応させて 示しており、論理が 明快。bore little resemblance to / failed to deliver what was advertised / whatsoever など C1 レベルの 語彙と、強いが 礼儀を 保った 語調が 高く 評価される。

passage: You are organising a street party for the people who live on your road.
question:
Write a letter to your neighbours.

In your letter
• explain the purpose of the party
• give details about the date, time and activities
• ask your neighbours to help in some way

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Neighbours,
answer:
Dear Neighbours,

I'm writing to invite you all to a street party on Willow Lane, which I'm organising together with a few other residents.

Many of us have lived here for years without really getting to know each other, and quite a few new families have moved in recently. We thought a party would be a great way to welcome them and to build a friendlier community spirit on our road.

The party will take place on Saturday 21 June, from 12 noon until 6 pm. The council has given us permission to close the road to traffic for the day. We are planning a shared lunch, a children's treasure hunt, a second-hand book swap and some live music from a local band. If it rains, we will move into the community hall at the end of the road.

To make the day a success, we'd really appreciate your help. Could you bring a dish of food to share, or perhaps lend us a table or some chairs? We also need a few volunteers to help set up in the morning. If you're able to help, please let me know at number 14.

Hope to see you there!

Best wishes,
Hannah Reid
explanation: 近所の 人々への セミフォーマルな 招待状として、目的・日時と 内容・協力の お願い を 漏れなく 書いている。雨天時の 対応まで 触れて いる 点や、Could you…? など 依頼の 表現の 自然さが 評価される。

passage: You missed a friend's birthday dinner last weekend.
question:
Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter
• apologise for missing the dinner
• explain why you could not go
• suggest a way to celebrate together soon

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Priya,
answer:
Dear Priya,

I'm so sorry I missed your birthday dinner on Saturday. I'd been looking forward to it for weeks, and I feel terrible that I wasn't there to celebrate with you.

I wanted to explain what happened. On Saturday morning, my grandmother had a fall at home, and my mum asked me to drive her to the hospital because my dad was away on business. We ended up waiting in the emergency department for most of the afternoon and evening. Thankfully, Gran only had a sprained wrist, but by the time we got her home and settled, it was nearly eleven o'clock. I should have called you earlier instead of just sending a short message, and I'm sorry about that too.

I'd really love to make it up to you. How about I take you out for lunch next weekend? You've always wanted to try that new Lebanese place by the river, so it would be my treat. Alternatively, we could go to the cinema and have dinner afterwards – whichever you prefer.

I hope you had a wonderful evening anyway.

Lots of love,
Elena
explanation: 謝罪 → 理由 → 埋め合わせの 提案 の 流れが 自然で、I should have called you… と 自分の 落ち度も 認める ことで 誠実な 語調に なっている。make it up to you / my treat など 口語的な 表現が インフォーマルな 手紙に ふさわしい。

passage: You cancelled your membership at a gym two months ago, but money is still being taken from your bank account.
question:

• describe the problem with the payments
• say what action you want the gym to take

Write at least 150 words.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing regarding my membership at your Eastgate branch (membership number 40719), which I cancelled in September but for which I am still being charged.

On 3 September, I visited the reception desk and completed the cancellation form, giving the required one month's notice. The member of staff who assisted me confirmed that my final payment would be taken on 1 October, and I received an email the same day acknowledging the cancellation, a copy of which I have attached.

Despite this, a further monthly payment of £42 was taken from my bank account on both 1 November and 1 December. When I phoned the gym in November to query the first of these, I was assured that the matter would be resolved, yet the second payment was taken regardless. Needless to say, I find this extremely frustrating, as I have not used the facilities since September.

I would therefore ask you to refund the two payments, totalling £84, within ten working days and to confirm in writing that no further payments will be taken. Should the problem continue, I will have no choice but to contact my bank to stop the payments.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Kowalski

passage: The bus stop near your home has recently been moved to a new location further away.
question:
Write a letter to the transport department of your local council.

In your letter
• describe the change that has been made
• explain the problems this has caused for local people
• suggest a solution

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing on behalf of several residents of Hillside Avenue to express our concern about the recent relocation of the number 27 bus stop.

Until last month, the stop was located outside the pharmacy at the corner of Hillside Avenue and Mill Street. However, it has now been moved approximately 600 metres further down the road, beyond the roundabout, without any notice being given to local residents.

This change has caused considerable difficulties. Many people in our area are elderly, and for them the walk to the new stop, which is uphill on the way back, is long and tiring. In addition, there is no shelter or seating at the new location, so passengers have to wait in the rain. Parents with pushchairs have also complained that they have to cross the busy roundabout to reach it.

We understand that the stop may have been moved because of traffic problems near the pharmacy. If that is the case, we would like to suggest placing it about 100 metres further along Mill Street, where the pavement is wide and there is room for a shelter.

I look forward to your response.

Yours faithfully,
Fatima Yusuf

passage: Your company has asked employees for ideas on how to improve the office.
question:
Write a letter to your manager.

In your letter
• describe a problem with the current office
• explain your idea for improving it
• say how this change would benefit staff and the company

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mr Adeyemi,
answer:
Dear Mr Adeyemi,

Following your recent request for suggestions on improving the office, I would like to put forward an idea that several colleagues and I have discussed.

Since we moved to the open-plan layout last year, many of us have found it difficult to concentrate. Phone calls, video meetings and conversations all take place in the same space, and with only two small meeting rooms that are almost always booked, there is nowhere to go for tasks that require focus.

My proposal is to convert the storage room next to the kitchen, which is currently only half used, into a "quiet room". It could be furnished with four or five desks and some comfortable chairs, and a simple rule could be introduced that no calls or conversations are allowed there. The items currently stored in it could be moved to the basement.

I believe this would benefit both staff and the company. Employees would have a place to work without interruption, which should improve both the quality of their work and their wellbeing. In turn, this could reduce errors and help the company retain staff. The cost would be minimal, as we already have spare furniture.

I would be happy to discuss this further.

Kind regards,
Sofia Marchetti
explanation: 問題 → 提案 → 利点 の 論理的な 流れで、コスト面まで 触れて 提案の 現実性を 示している。put forward an idea / In turn / retain staff など ビジネスに 適した 語彙と、上司宛ての 丁寧な 語調の バランスが C1 として 評価される。

passage: You are going away for a week and need someone to look after your cat.
question:
Write a letter to a friend.

In your letter
• explain where you are going and why
• give instructions about how to look after your cat
• offer something in return for their help

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sam,
answer:
Dear Sam,

How are you? I hope your new job is going well. I'm writing because I need to ask you a big favour.

Next week I'm going to Lisbon for my cousin's wedding. I'll be away from Monday 8th to Sunday 14th, and my usual cat-sitter is on holiday at the same time. Would you be able to look after Biscuit for me while I'm away?

Don't worry, it's quite easy! She needs one small bowl of dry food in the morning and half a tin of wet food in the evening. Please give her fresh water every day too. Her litter tray is in the bathroom, and it needs to be cleaned every two days. She's very friendly, but please don't let her go outside, because she's not used to the area yet. I'll leave the spare key with my neighbour at number 6.

To say thank you, I'd love to take you out for dinner when I come back. I'll also bring you back some of those Portuguese custard tarts you like!

Let me know if you can help.

Thanks a lot,
Maya

passage: You ordered some furniture from a shop, but it has not been delivered on the agreed date.
question:
Write a letter to the shop.

In your letter
• describe what you ordered and when it should have been delivered
• explain the problems the delay has caused
• say what you want the shop to do

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the delivery of an order I placed with your store on 10 April (order number HF-28813).

I bought a three-seater grey sofa and a matching armchair, for which I paid £1,150 in full at the time of purchase. I was told that the items would be delivered on Saturday 3 May between 8 am and 1 pm. However, nobody arrived, and when I phoned your customer service line that afternoon, I was simply told that there had been a "delay at the warehouse" and that I would be contacted. I have heard nothing since.

This delay has caused me a number of problems. I took a day off work to wait for the delivery, which I cannot easily do again. Moreover, I had already arranged for a charity to collect my old sofa, so I now have nowhere to sit in my living room, and I have relatives coming to stay next weekend.

I would therefore like you to confirm a new delivery date within the next seven days. If this is not possible, I expect a full refund. I would also appreciate some compensation for the inconvenience.

Yours faithfully,
Chen Wei

passage: You are applying for a job and need a reference from a teacher who taught you a few years ago.
question:
Write a letter to your former teacher.

In your letter
• remind the teacher who you are
• give details of the job you are applying for
• explain what you would like the teacher to include in the reference

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Dr Nakamura,
answer:
Dear Dr Nakamura,

I hope this letter finds you well. You may remember me from your environmental science classes at Westbrook College, where I studied between 2020 and 2022. I was the student who organised the river clean-up project for our final-year assessment, which you supervised.

I am writing because I am applying for a position as a field research assistant with a conservation charity that monitors water quality in wetlands. The role involves collecting samples, recording data and occasionally presenting findings to local community groups. I was wondering whether you would be willing to act as one of my referees.

If you agree, it would be extremely helpful if you could comment on my practical skills in the field and my ability to work independently, as these are both emphasised in the job description. It would also be useful if you could mention the clean-up project, since it demonstrates my experience of planning and leading a team.

The charity has asked for references by 30 June. I have enclosed a copy of the job description and my current CV for your information.

Thank you very much for considering my request.

Yours sincerely,
Isabel Moreno
explanation: 先生に 思い出して もらう ための 具体的な 手がかり（授業名・年・プロジェクト）を 示し、推薦状に 書いて ほしい 点を 求人内容と 結びつけて いる 点が 高度。I was wondering whether you would be willing to… など 遠回しで 丁寧な 依頼表現が C1 の 語調として 評価される。

passage: You recently went on a guided walking tour of a city, and the tour guide was excellent.
question:
Write a letter to the tour company.

In your letter
• give details of the tour you went on
• explain what the guide did that was so good
• suggest how the company could reward the guide

Write at least 150 words.
You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to express my appreciation for the "Hidden Streets" walking tour I took with your company in Valletta on 22 August, which was led by a guide called Joseph.

The tour lasted about three hours and took our group of twelve through the narrow lanes of the old city, including several small churches and courtyards that I would never have found on my own.

What made the experience so memorable was Joseph himself. He was extremely knowledgeable and brought the history of each building to life with amusing stories and local legends. He also made a real effort to include everyone: he spoke slowly for those of us whose English is not perfect, and he walked at a gentle pace for an elderly couple in the group. When it started to rain, he quickly changed the route so that we could visit an indoor market instead.

I strongly believe Joseph deserves recognition for his work. Perhaps you could feature him on your website as "Guide of the Month" or give him a bonus. I will certainly be recommending your company to my friends.

Yours faithfully,
Anna Weber
explanation: ほめる 手紙では 具体的な エピソード（ゆっくり 話す・高齢者に 合わせる・雨で ルート変更）が 説得力の 鍵で、Task Achievement を 大きく 高める。brought… to life / deserves recognition など 評価の 語彙も 豊か。
